behavior: New process starts unauthenticated. Prior durable refresh records are retired into the original issuer revocation queue, never refreshed into login.

Main-window close preserves the existing global draft/unknown-submission guards, retires local login before the first network await and grants issuer revocation a three-second bound. Minimize preserves login.

Authenticated owner maintains one automatic GET /auth/session/watch with a 35-second response budget; authoritative replacement retires current login and shows the server device reason without a manual refresh.
Automatic watch, fallback me and their token refresh do not renew human activity. A missing watch endpoint falls back to a three-second me probe and retries watch after 60 seconds.
Read, refresh, mutation, download and watch rejection share one generation-fenced SessionEnded event. Late/cancelled responses cannot clear or notify a new login.

InputManager lifetime tracking records timestamps only for keyboard/IME/mouse/touch/stylus input in the main owner or owned dialogs. A single-flight 30-second staff me pulse renews activity only when input was observed in the last 30 seconds.
Session changed/read-scope/ended publication isolates each listener exception and logs only technical event/type metadata; one failing subscriber cannot suppress other cleanup or replacement notices.

Native publish retirement runs on its Dispatcher. Latest undebounced input and retired/disposed snapshots persist through the immutable original namespace lease. Storage failure retains a global main-window close guard; retry has an owned wait window, repeat-click guard and background DPAPI/disk IO.
Retired publish queues stop after every read/prepare/upload/publish/withdraw await; delayed success or failure cannot replace Unknown original request IDs or advance the old queue.

limitations: Offline transport and real local WPF windows only; no live company authentication was exercised.
A closed/offline/killed process cannot guarantee immediate server-side revocation; issuer-bound pending revocations are retained and never restored into local login.
